parts.title: Plan a weekend away
parts.instructions: Read what each person is looking for. Match each person to the best activity. There are three extra activities.

people.text: Anouk has never been on a boat and would like to try something on the water on Saturday morning.
Bruno loves old streets and castles and wants a guided tour so that he can hear stories about the town.
Cleo is travelling with two young children and needs a free activity for a rainy day.
Dmitri enjoys good food and wants to taste dishes made with local ingredients.
Esme is very active and wants a long walk with great views of the coast.

texts.title: Old town walking tour
texts.text: Follow a local guide through narrow streets and hear stories about the castle, the harbour and the market. Tours leave daily at 11 a.m. and last 90 minutes.

texts.title: Family library morning
texts.text: Rainy day? Come to the town library for free story time, drawing and games for children under ten. Open all weekend.

texts.title: Beginner kayaking
texts.text: Never paddled before? Our friendly instructors will teach you the basics on the calm bay. Saturday and Sunday mornings, equipment included.

texts.title: Pottery workshop
texts.text: Make your own cup or plate in a two-hour class. Choose your colours and we will post your work to you after it has been fired.

texts.title: Harbour food market
texts.text: Taste cheese, fish and bread from nearby farms and boats. You can watch cooks prepare dishes and try them before you buy. Saturdays only.

texts.title: Beach stroll
texts.text: Enjoy a short, flat walk along the sand with views of the coast. It takes about forty minutes.

texts.title: Cliff path walk
texts.text: Walk twelve kilometres along the high cliffs and enjoy views of the whole coast. Wear strong shoes; there are no cafés on the way.

texts.title: Lighthouse tour
texts.text: A guide takes small groups to the top of the lighthouse and tells stories about the sailors. Tours at 2 p.m. on Sundays.

parts.title: A weekend by the sea
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, my cousin invited me to spend a weekend in a small seaside town. We travelled by coach because it was cheaper than the train, although the journey took longer. When we arrived, the weather was cloudy, so we visited the local museum first. I expected it to be rather boring, but a guide showed us old photographs of the harbour and explained how the fishing boats had changed over time.

The next morning was sunny. We hired bicycles and followed a path along the coast. The route was mostly flat, but we stopped several times to take photographs. At lunchtime, we bought sandwiches from a small shop and ate them on the beach. It was busy, but we found a quiet place near the rocks.

On Sunday, we planned to take a boat trip. Unfortunately, the sea was too rough, so the trip was cancelled. The owner gave everyone a refund and suggested a walk to a lighthouse instead. I was disappointed at first, but the view from the top was wonderful. I would happily return, especially if I could stay for a few more days.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer travel by coach?
options: It was nearer to her cousin's house.
questions.explanation: The coach was cheaper than the train, so it was less expensive.

questions.prompt: What surprised the writer at the museum?
questions.explanation: She expected the museum to be boring, but the guide showed interesting old photographs, so she was surprised how interesting it was.

questions.prompt: What did they do on the coast path?
options: They had lunch in a cafe.
questions.explanation: They stopped several times to take photographs along the coast path.

questions.prompt: Why was the boat trip cancelled?
options: The weather at sea was unsafe.
questions.explanation: The sea was too rough, so the weather at sea was unsafe.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about the weekend?
options: They did not enjoy the town.
They would like a longer visit.
They want to travel by train next time.
They want to move to the town.
questions.explanation: She says she would happily return and stay for a few more days, so she would like a longer visit.

parts.title: The coastal path
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage: The coastal path is popular with visitors and local people, especially in spring and summer. [1] It begins near the old harbour and continues past a small museum. [2] The town has added signs so walkers can find the route easily, and volunteers clean the path every month. There are benches at several points, and most of the path is flat. [3] Some families bring a picnic and stop beside the beach. Dogs are welcome, but they must stay on a lead near the farms. The final section goes uphill towards a lighthouse. [4] On clear days, you can see several islands from the top. The council hopes to extend the path next year. [5]
sentences: It is steep in places, but the climb is worth it.
In winter, the wind can be very strong near the cliffs.
It is about eight kilometres long and takes most people three hours.
More walkers would then be able to reach the next village on foot.
Many walkers stop there to look at old photographs of the harbour.
This makes it a good walk for families with young children.
Fishing is not allowed from the rocks near the lighthouse.
We decided to stay indoors all afternoon.

gaps.explanation: “It is about eight kilometres long” gives the first facts about the path and leads to “It begins near the old harbour”.
“Many walkers stop there to look at old photographs” follows “a small museum” (“there”) and leads to the signs.
“This makes it a good walk for families” follows “most of the path is flat” and leads to families bringing a picnic.
“It is steep in places, but the climb is worth it” follows the uphill section and leads to the view from the top.
“More walkers would then be able to reach the next village” follows the hope to extend the path.

parts.title: A day trip by train
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word or phrase for each gap.
parts.passage: Many families [1] a day trip by train during the school holidays. It is useful to [2] the timetable before leaving home. Some tickets are [3] expensive if you book early. The station is [4] the town centre, so visitors can walk to the shops. If it rains, you can [5] the local museum. Children usually enjoy the journey as much as the destination. Remember to [6] a bottle of water for the journey.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: You check a timetable before leaving home.

questions.prompt: Gap 4

parts.title: A day at the coast
parts.instructions: Complete the text with one word in each gap.
parts.passage: We arrived [1] the coast before lunchtime. The weather was warmer [2] we had expected, so we left our coats in the car. My sister wanted to swim, [3] the water was too cold. We spent an hour looking [4] the boats in the harbour. After lunch we walked along the beach and collected shells. Later, we found a café [5] served fresh sandwiches. It was a day [6] we will remember for a long time.

gaps.explanation: We say “arrive at” a place such as the coast.
“Warmer than we had expected” is a comparison.
“But” shows the contrast between wanting to swim and the cold water.
“Looking at the boats” means watching them.
“That” refers to the café and begins the clause “that served fresh sandwiches”.
“Which” (or “that”) refers to the day and begins the clause about remembering it.

turns.speaker: nathan
turns.text: Hello. Is it true that the museum closes at five? That’s what the website says.

turns.speaker: olivia
turns.text: It used to, yes. But from this month we stay open until eight on Fridays.

turns.speaker: nathan
turns.text: Oh good. I was told this morning that it’s closed today for a private event.

turns.speaker: olivia
turns.text: Only the café. And the clock room, which was shut last month, is open again, so you can see everything.

turns.speaker: nathan
turns.text: Then I’ll come at six, after work.

turns.speaker: olivia
turns.text: Perfect. Tickets are half price after five.

options: The last room is not open.
The museum closes later than expected.
question.explanation: The website says the museum closes at five, but Olivia says that on Fridays it stays open until eight; only the café is closed and the clock room is open again.

turns.speaker: rafael
turns.text: The film starts at eight. Shall we meet at seven?

turns.speaker: elsa
turns.text: Seven is too early. We only need to collect the tickets.

turns.speaker: rafael
turns.text: There might be a queue at the box office.

turns.speaker: elsa
turns.text: I bought them online, so there’s no queue. My bus gets in at six forty, so I could be there early, but I’ll have a coffee first.

turns.text: Got everything for the pool, Cathy?

turns.speaker: cathy
turns.text: Let me think. Swimming costume, goggles. I put the car keys in my pocket. They’re here.

turns.speaker: ivan
turns.text: And your camera? You said you’d film Tom.

turns.speaker: cathy

turns.speaker: ivan

turns.speaker: cathy

turns.speaker: bridget
turns.text: Are you doing anything on Sunday, Jamal? We’re going for a walk in the forest.

turns.speaker: jamal
turns.text: Sounds nice, but I’ve promised my nephew a day out. We were going to take the train to the coast, but he’d rather see the fish, so we’re booking the aquarium instead.

turns.text: I’ll tell Dad to come at ten.

turns.speaker: lucas

turns.speaker: kim

turns.speaker: lucas

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: How was your trip to the lake, Dora?

turns.speaker: dora

parts.title: A welcome talk at a hostel
parts.instructions: Listen and complete the notes. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time in each gap.

turns.speaker: manager
turns.text: Welcome to the Hilltop Hostel. My name is Jess, and I’m the manager. Let me explain a few things before you go to your rooms. First, safety. The front door is locked after eleven at night. Last week we had a problem with the old system, which locked at ten, but the new one is working. So please take your key with you if you go out for the evening. Breakfast is served in the dining room from half past seven. It was at seven in the past, but the cook asked for extra time to prepare. It finishes at ten, and there’s tea, coffee, bread and fruit. Now, the best activity here is our morning walk to the old castle. Mr Green will lead it. He has lived in the village all his life, and he knows every path. Some guests think the leader is Mr Brown, but he only helps in the summer. The walk takes about two hours, with a stop for photos halfway, and you don’t need special shoes. It leaves from the front steps at nine thirty. If you want to go into town afterwards, you can leave your bags beside reception. Please don’t leave them in the hall, because it blocks the way, and the cleaners will move them. We aren’t responsible for money or phones, so keep those with you. Finally, the bus into town stops at the bottom of the hill. Buses leave every twenty minutes during the day, but in the evening they are only once an hour. The last bus is at ten forty. Enjoy your stay, and please ask us if you have any questions.

gaps.prompt: The front door is locked at night after ___
gaps.explanation: Jess says the new system locks after eleven; the old one locked at ten.

gaps.prompt: Breakfast is served from half past ___
gaps.explanation: Breakfast used to start at seven, but now it starts at half past seven.

gaps.prompt: The walk to the castle is led by Mr ___
gaps.explanation: She says Mr Green leads it; Mr Brown only helps in the summer.
The walk takes about two hours, with a stop for photos halfway.

gaps.prompt: You can leave your bags ___ (not in the hall)
gaps.explanation: She says to leave bags beside reception and not in the hall.

gaps.prompt: In the daytime a bus leaves every ___ minutes
gaps.explanation: Buses leave every twenty minutes in the day; in the evening it is once an hour.

parts.title: An interview with a hostel owner
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Carlos, you run a successful hostel by the harbour. Why did you open it?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: I know people expect a long family story, but I didn’t take over a hotel from my parents, my family worked in a factory. And I didn’t need a job near the harbour either, I had one in an office. What happened is that I travelled for a year in my twenties, and I stayed in some wonderful places where strangers became friends in one evening. I wanted to bring that warm feeling to my own town.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Why did you choose the old building?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: It’s not next to the railway station, in fact it’s a twenty-minute walk. And when I bought it, it was empty, so I had to buy all the furniture myself. But it was cheap, because nobody wanted it, and it had lots of room for beds. I could have found something nicer, but I couldn’t have found anything bigger at that price.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What’s the hardest part of running it?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: Summer weekends. The rooms are quite big, so groups are fine, and my staff don’t take holidays then, I won’t allow it! The problem is that guests often arrive much earlier than they said. They get off the night bus at six in the morning and we have nothing ready, so I spend a lot of those mornings making beds.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do guests enjoy most?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: They like watching the boats in the harbour, of course, and the breakfast is nice, although it isn’t free, it’s included in the price. But what people write about in the comments is the roof terrace. They sit up there in the evening, talk and watch the sunset, and that’s when they get to know each other.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Was it easy to make money?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: Not in the first month, definitely. We lost money for a long time. It took about two years before I could pay myself a proper salary, and I nearly gave up in the second winter. But it was worth waiting.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What advice would you give someone who wants to open a hostel?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: Don’t try to do it alone. You can save money that way, but you’ll be exhausted. And you don’t need the biggest building in town, I know I said it helps. The most useful thing is to ask your guests what they like, and then change things. I’ve learned more from conversations than from books.

questions.prompt: Why did Carlos open a hostel?
options: He took over a family hotel
He wanted to share the warm welcome he enjoyed
He needed a job near the harbour
questions.explanation: Carlos did not inherit a hotel or need a job; he wanted to bring the warm feeling he found as a traveller to his own town.

questions.prompt: Why did Carlos choose the old building?
options: It was next to the station
It cost little and had room
questions.explanation: The building was far from the station and empty, but it was cheap and had lots of room for beds.

questions.prompt: What is difficult about summer weekends?
options: Guests often arrive earlier than expected.
The rooms are too small for groups.
Many of the staff are on holiday.
questions.explanation: Staff holidays and room size are not the problem; the difficulty on summer weekends is that guests arrive earlier than they said.

questions.prompt: What do guests enjoy most?
questions.explanation: Guests like the boats and the breakfast, but the comments praise the roof terrace where they talk and watch the sunset.

questions.prompt: What does Carlos say about making money?
options: It happened in the first month.
